newsitem.title: BURKINA FASO: French CFD gives loan to Burkina Faso cotton firm.
newsitem.headline: French CFD gives loan to Burkina Faso cotton firm.

text.p: France's Caisse Francaise de Developpement (CFD) has given Burkina Faso's state cotton firm SOFITEX a four billion CFA loan to help build a cotton ginning factory at Solenzo near the border with Mali, officials said.
The factory would be able to separate the seed and fibres from about 20,000 tonnes of seed cotton a year, SOFITEX press officer Gilbert Koboru told Reuters on Friday.
The loan was repayable over seven years after a two-year grace period.
It brings the CFD's loans to SOFITEX to eight billion CFA and France's total loans to the country's cotton sector to 25 billion CFA over the last 10 years.

This has helped SOFITEX improve its infrastructure and build other new ginning factories, like the 3,000-tonne unit opened at Banfora last April. This plant brought national ginning capacity to 140,000 tonnes.
Burkina Faso has launched a five-year plan to boost seed cotton output to 345,000 tonnes in 2000/01 from 151,200 tonnes this year.
It aims to grow 200,000 tonnes next season, 240,000 tonnes in 1997/98, 264,000 tonnes in 1998/99 and 300,000 tonnes in 1999/2000.
SOFITEX's turnover is expected to rise from 53 billion CFA to 124 billion in this period.
SOFITEX has said it will pay producers 180 CFA a kg for top grade seed cotton next season against 165 CFA this year.
The government signed the Solenzo loan deal with the CFD last Thursday, Koboru said.
